title: Clarinetists: the Baquets, Big Eye Louis, Tio, Dodds and Barney Bigard
summary: He names the great clarinet players, explains the nickname Hooks for Johnny Dodds, and remembers Barney Bigard as a boy watching his father roll cigars.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: That's fine. How about clarinets?
Clarinets?
So many great clarinets in the world, players from New Orleans.
All right, we start off right now with Georgie Baquet --
Ah? Huh?
You ain't heard that name in quite a while, have you? That's one of the ace.
That's right.
That's right. I call, Achille Baquet,
that's his brother.
Right.
Good clarinet man. I call Big Eye Louie, which is Louis Nelson. I call Lorenzo Tio. George McCullen -- not George McCullen, yeah, George McCullen, clarinet man. I call -- good clarinet players -- oh,
Johnny Dodds?
Johnny Dodds, I leave old Hooks out. I forgot about old Hooks.
Hooks, you call him Hooks?

Hooks, cause his legs hooks around.
I don't know that name, okay?
Yeah, Johnny Dodds is all right.
That's it.
How about Barney Bigard?
